authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Sustain - Formal Execution.md, §VI (Viab_T(V) — the viability kernel); 3B1B — Operative - Formal Execution.md, §X (runway as the viability term with a clock)
note: SPEC vectors for the viability kernel and runway. Authored from the articles, not generated from the reference engine.

divergence.statement: Neither the kernel nor runway exists in the reference. The Operative article's own Note says it precisely: 'Viab / viability_kernel — grep-0; no kernel anywhere. Hence no runway: burn_rate_analysis.json computes a RATE, not an exit time R(s) against V — and cannot, because V is not yet a region to exit.'

term_by_term.Viab_T(V): RUST-AHEAD. grep-0. The reference has no notion of 'can this keep going', only 'is this valid now'. Its invariants answer membership in V; nothing answers membership in the set you can STAY in.
term_by_term.runway R(s): RUST-AHEAD. burn_rate_analysis.json computes a rate of spend — a slope, not an exit time. A rate says how fast; runway says WHEN, and only the second one is a point of no return.
term_by_term.the kernel margin: RUST-AHEAD, and it upgrades something Rust itself shipped last slice: region.rs's margin() measures distance to the edge of V, which is an honest OVER-estimate because the kernel is a subset of V and its edge is never further away.
term_by_term.descent toward the kernel: RUST-AHEAD, and it sharpens CTL-2. Lyapunov descent toward V says the household is closer to being alive today; descent toward the kernel says it is closer to being able to STAY alive. A vector shows a move that reduces nothing about W and improves the box margin while walking out of the kernel.

divergence.what_python_does_have_and_why_it_is_not_: burn_rate_analysis is a real, shipped sub-operative graph, and a burn rate is genuinely useful — it is the thing most household finance tools show. What it cannot do is name a date. The article's framing is that promoting a burn rate to a runway needs V as a region, which arrived in the previous slice; this is the promotion.
divergence.scoping_stated_plainly: §VI names two honest limitations and BOTH are encoded rather than worked around. (1) Exact kernels are exponential in the dimensions, so the exact computation here runs over an EXPLICITLY ENUMERATED space — genuinely Viab_T(V) for the space it was given, with no claim about states nobody enumerated. (2) The finite-horizon Viab^H is a SUPERSET of the true kernel, so a horizon answer is OPTIMISTIC — encoded as a separate Kernel::Horizon variant with no constructor that turns it into Kernel::Exact. Reporting an optimistic set as a guarantee is unspellable, not merely discouraged.
divergence.when_python_catches_up: These cases become parity vectors unchanged; nothing in them is Rust-specific.
divergence.not_a_divergence_in: R1 behaviour. The kernel is a new additive module and touches no existing gate path.

space.why: A discretised ledger. `earn` tops up while under a ceiling; `spend` draws down between a floor and that ceiling. Above the ceiling both moves are blocked — funds locked away — which is what makes the kernel a PROPER subset of V rather than trivially equal to it.

kernel_cases.name: the_kernel_is_a_proper_subset_of_v
kernel_cases.why: THE distinction the module exists for. b30 satisfies `balance >= 0`, so it IS in V — and every move is blocked there, so no sequence keeps it going. In V, outside the kernel: fine right now, already lost.

kernel_cases.name: a_state_whose_every_move_leads_somewhere_deleted_is_deleted_too
kernel_cases.why: The cascade of the descending iteration. With only `spend`, b0 goes first (no admissible move), then b10 follows it out, then b20 — each pass deleting the states whose every legal move leads somewhere already deleted.

kernel_cases.name: a_cycle_survives_forever
kernel_cases.why: b10 ⇄ b20 under earn/spend is a genuine ω-trajectory — some sequence of legal moves, forever, which is exactly what the definition asks for.

kernel_cases.name: an_opaque_move_is_refused_rather_than_skipped
kernel_cases.why: A move nobody described cannot be simulated, so it cannot be part of a survival claim. Skipping it would quietly shrink T and make the kernel look SMALLER than it is — a pessimistic lie is still a lie.

horizon_cases.name: a_horizon_answer_is_never_a_guarantee
horizon_cases.why: Surviving H steps is easier than surviving forever, so Viab^H is optimistic. Encoded in the type: Kernel::Horizon has no constructor that turns it into Kernel::Exact, so the optimism cannot be dropped on the way to a caller.

horizon_cases.name: the_horizon_set_contains_the_true_kernel
horizon_cases.why: Viab^H ⊇ Viab_T(V), for every H. Checked at several horizons rather than asserted once — an approximation that was ever PESSIMISTIC would be the dangerous kind.

horizon_cases.name: a_longer_horizon_is_never_looser
horizon_cases.why: More looking only removes. The sequence of Viab^H is monotonically decreasing toward the true kernel.

runway_cases.name: fine_today_and_already_lost_by_thursday
runway_cases.why: THE PROOF OF VALUE, and the article's own example. The household is comfortably inside V — W = 0, box margin 500 — and rent falls due on Thursday whether or not anyone acts. R(s) = 4. Sustena's job is to say that on Monday.

runway_cases.name: a_solvent_household_survives_the_scan
runway_cases.why: The ordinary path — but note what is and is not claimed.

runway_cases.name: surviving_the_scan_is_not_a_promise
runway_cases.why: The horizon running out is the absence of evidence, not evidence of absence — which is why `steps` is None rather than infinity. The same household, looked at further, has a real number.

runway_cases.name: already_outside_is_a_runway_of_zero_not_an_absence
runway_cases.why: Zero is a real answer, and reporting it as 'no runway' would be the same number dressed as a missing one.

runway_cases.name: repeated_obligations_accumulate
runway_cases.why: One forward scan, one policy — the whole reason runway is cheap. 250 survives two hundreds, not three.

margin_cases.name: the_kernel_margin_is_tighter_than_the_box_margin
margin_cases.why: The upgrade. region.rs's margin() measures distance to the edge of V — an honest OVER-estimate, as it was labelled when it shipped. The kernel margin measures distance to the edge of the set you can STAY in, which is nearer.

margin_cases.name: a_state_outside_the_kernel_has_no_margin
margin_cases.why: Outside the kernel the question is runway, not room.

stability_cases.name: a_move_can_reduce_w_and_still_abandon_the_kernel
stability_cases.why: THE reason descent toward the kernel is the stronger condition, and the sharpening of CTL-2. b20 → b30 leaves W unchanged at 0 and IMPROVES the box margin (30 above the floor rather than 20) — and walks out of the set the household could have stayed in. The Lyapunov test sees an improvement; the kernel test sees the point of no return.

stability_cases.name: re_entering_the_kernel_is_stable_too
stability_cases.why: Ending inside is what matters — the condition is about where you land, not where you started.
